examples.en: Let us suppose it is raining.

examples.ko: 내가 부자라고 가정하면 뭘 할 거예요?
examples.en: If you suppose I am rich, what would you do?
The teacher assumed a problem situation.
I prepare by assuming the worst case.
What is the reason you assumed that?
First I will assume I fail the exam.

explain: 사실인지 모르지만 일단 그렇다고 치고 생각할 때 써요. '만약'이나 '-다면'과 비슷하지만, '가정하다'는 생각의 출발점을 정하는 말이에요. 명사 '가정'은 '가족'이나 '집'의 뜻도 있어서 헷갈리기 쉬워요.
explain_en: You use it when you do not know whether something is true but think as if it were. It is close to '만약' and '-다면', but '가정하다' sets up the starting point of your thinking. The noun '가정' also means a household, so it is easy to confuse.

examples.en: I stopped for a moment at the fork while walking along the mountain path.

examples.ko: 저 갈림길을 지나서 오른쪽으로 가면 시장이 나와요.
examples.en: If you pass that fork and go right, you will reach the market.

examples.ko: 지도를 봐도 어느 갈림길이 맞는지 몰랐어요.
examples.en: Even with the map, I did not know which fork was the right one.
That choice was a turning point in my life.

examples.ko: 갈림길마다 표지판이 있어서 길을 잃지 않았어요.
examples.en: There was a sign at every fork, so I did not get lost.

examples.ko: 지금은 회사를 옮길지 말지 갈림길에 서 있어요.
examples.en: Right now I am at a crossroads about whether to change companies.

explain: 갈림길은 길이 둘로 갈라지는 곳이에요. 길이 만나는 모양을 정확히 말할 때는 '삼거리', '사거리'를 써요. '갈림길에 서다'처럼 인생의 중요한 선택 앞에서도 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 졸업을 앞두고 진로 갈림길에 서 있어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이 아니라 인생의 중요한 선택을 앞두었다는 비유예요. 진로, 이직, 결혼 같은 큰 결정에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for facing an important life choice such as career, changing jobs, or marriage, not an actual road.

explain_en: 갈림길 is a spot where a road splits in two. When you need the exact shape of a junction, you say 삼거리 or 사거리. People also say 갈림길에 서다 when they face a big life decision.

examples.en: I tapped my card at the subway gate and went in.
I'll wait for my friend in front of the ticket gate.

examples.ko: 표가 없으면 개찰구를 통과할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Without a ticket, you can't get through the gate.
During rush hour every gate is crowded.
My card wouldn't register at the gate, and I panicked.
Strollers have to go through the wide gate.

explain: 지하철이나 기차역에서 표나 교통카드를 확인하고 지나가는 곳이에요. 표를 사는 곳은 '매표소'라고 해서 서로 짝이 돼요. 보통 '개찰구를 통과하다', '개찰구에서 찍다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is the gate at a subway or train station where your ticket or transit card is checked. The place where you buy tickets is a '매표소', so the two go together. People say '개찰구를 통과하다' or '개찰구에서 찍다'.

examples.en: I spread a little mustard on the sandwich.
Mustard sauce has a sharp, pungent taste.
Cold-dish salads are served with mustard sauce.
The mustard was so hot that my nose stung.
I sprayed both ketchup and mustard on the hot dog.
The mustard taste goes up to the tip of my nose.

explain: 식당에서는 '겨자 소스'나 '연겨자'로 자주 보고, 초밥의 '와사비'와 달리 노란색이에요. 고추의 매운맛과 달리 코로 올라오는 매운맛이라서 '코가 찡하다'와 같이 말해요. 한국에서는 냉채나 냉면에 곁들이기도 해요.
explain_en: At restaurants you often see it as '겨자 소스' or '연겨자', and unlike sushi's '와사비' it is yellow. Its heat goes up the nose rather than burning the tongue like chili, so people say '코가 찡하다'. In Korea it is also served with cold salads and cold noodles.

examples.ko: 보물 상자 안에 금화가 가득 들어 있었어요.
examples.en: The treasure chest was full of gold coins.
In the old days people paid with gold coins.
They say the pirates hid gold coins.

examples.ko: 게임에서 금화를 모으면 아이템을 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: In the game, you can buy items if you collect gold coins.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 천 년 된 금화를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a thousand-year-old gold coin at the museum.

examples.ko: 금화 한 닢이 얼마나 되는지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder how much one gold coin is worth.

explain: '금화'는 금으로 만든 동전이에요. 은으로 만든 건 '은화', 지금 쓰는 동전은 '동전'이라고 해요. 옛이야기나 게임에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: 금화 is a coin made of gold. A silver one is 은화, and the coins used today are just 동전. It shows up often in old tales and games.

examples.en: The kids roll a lump of snow to make a snowman.
The interest piled up and the debt snowballed.

examples.ko: 언덕 위에서 눈덩이가 아래로 굴러 내려왔어요.
examples.en: A big lump of snow rolled down from the top of the hill.
Even a small lump of snow gets bigger if you keep rolling it.
I packed a snowball with my hands and threw it at my friend.

examples.ko: 걱정이 눈덩이처럼 커져서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My worries snowballed and I couldn't sleep.

explain: 눈을 뭉치거나 굴려서 만든 덩어리예요. 놀이에서는 '눈뭉치'라고도 해요. 비유로 더 많이 쓰여서 '눈덩이처럼 불어나다/커지다'가 자주 나와요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 빚, 피해, 걱정 같은 것이 빠르게 점점 커질 때 써요. 보통 좋지 않은 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things like debt, damage or worry grow rapidly. It is usually about bad things.

explain_en: It is a lump of snow that is packed or rolled. For play, people also say '눈뭉치'. It is used a lot figuratively, as in '눈덩이처럼 불어나다/커지다'.

examples.ko: 가게 앞에 마네킹 세 개가 서 있어요.
examples.en: Three mannequins are standing in front of the shop.
Try dressing the mannequin in the new clothes.

examples.ko: 그 모델은 마네킹처럼 키가 크고 말랐어요.
examples.en: That model is tall and thin like a mannequin.

examples.ko: 쇼윈도의 마네킹을 보고 같은 옷을 샀어요.
examples.en: I saw the mannequin in the shop window and bought the same outfit.

examples.ko: 점원이 마네킹이 입은 옷과 같은 옷을 가져왔어요.
examples.en: The clerk brought the same outfit the mannequin was wearing.
We practice first aid on a mannequin.

explain: 옷가게에서 '마네킹이 입은 옷 주세요'라고 말하면 점원이 바로 알아들어요. 응급 처치 연습용 사람 모형도 마네킹이라고 해요. 표정 없이 가만히 서 있는 사람에게 '마네킹 같다'고 놀리기도 해요.
explain_en: In a clothing store, saying '마네킹이 입은 옷 주세요' gets you the outfit on display. First-aid practice dummies are also called 마네킹. People tease someone standing still without expression by saying '마네킹 같다'.

examples.en: He reflected on his mistake and apologized.
I look back at today and reflect on it.
He seemed to regret having lied.

examples.ko: 반성한 사람에게는 한 번 더 기회를 줘요.
examples.en: We give one more chance to a person who has reflected.
After botching the exam, I reflected on how I study.
If there is something you need to reflect on, say it honestly.

explain: '반성'은 속으로 돌아보며 잘못을 느끼는 것이고, '사과'는 상대에게 말로 하는 거예요. 학교나 직장에서 '반성하고 있어요'라는 말을 들을 수 있어요. '반성을 하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: '반성' is looking back inwardly and feeling your mistake, while '사과' (apology) is said to the other person. You may hear '반성하고 있어요' at school or work. It also works as the noun plus 하다: '반성을 하다'.

examples.ko: 전화도 못 드리고 지내는 게 큰 불효 같아요.
examples.en: It feels like a great failure of filial duty that I can't even call my parents.
Many people regret their lack of filial duty only now.
Making your parents worry is also unfilial.
I am an unfilial child, so I always feel sorry to my parents.

examples.ko: 불효는 작은 무심함에서 시작될 때가 많아요.
examples.en: Unfilial behavior often starts with small acts of neglect.

examples.ko: 불효에 대한 미안함 때문에 고향에 내려갔어요.
examples.en: I went down to my hometown because I felt sorry for not being a good child.

explain: 반대말은 '효도'예요. 부모님께 잘 못했다고 자신을 돌아보거나 미안해할 때 자주 써요. 부모를 잘 모시지 못하는 자식은 '불효자'라고 해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '효도'. It is often used when reflecting on or feeling sorry for not treating one's parents well. A child who fails to care for their parents is called '불효자'.

examples.ko: 마트에서 새로 나온 주스를 시음해 봤어요.
examples.en: I sampled the new juice at the supermarket.

examples.ko: 오늘 카페에서 신메뉴 시음 행사를 해요.
examples.en: The cafe is holding a tasting event for new menu items today.

examples.ko: 사기 전에 먼저 시음할 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can I taste it before I buy?
Many people were sampling, so the line was long.
I tried the tea, and the aroma was really good.

examples.ko: 이 매장은 시음용 작은 컵도 줘요.
examples.en: This store also gives you small cups for tasting.

explain: 마시는 것에 써요. 먹어 보는 음식은 '시식하다'라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. 마트나 카페에서 '시음 행사', '시음회'처럼 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used for drinks. For food you try, the matching word is '시식하다', so learn them as a pair. You often see it in '시음 행사' and '시음회' at supermarkets and cafes.

examples.en: I sliced the button mushrooms thinly and sautéed them in butter.
The mushroom soup is smooth and really delicious.
Please put button mushrooms on the pizza too.
I bought a pack of button mushrooms at the mart.

examples.ko: 양송이는 물에 오래 담그지 말고 살짝 씻으세요.
examples.en: Don't soak button mushrooms in water; just rinse them lightly.
I made cream pasta with button mushrooms.

explain: '양송이버섯'을 줄인 말이에요. 갓이 하얗고 동그래서 수프, 피자, 파스타에 잘 어울려요. 표고나 느타리처럼 한국 요리에 흔한 버섯과 구분해서 말해요.
explain_en: It is the short form of '양송이버섯'. Its cap is white and round, so it suits soups, pizza and pasta. People distinguish it from mushrooms common in Korean cooking, like 표고 and 느타리.

examples.en: The two who had broken up finally got back together.
That band will reunite next year.
There are cases where a divorced couple gets back together.

examples.ko: 그 그룹이 재결합하자 팬들이 크게 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: When the group reunited, fans were overjoyed.

examples.ko: 갈라섰던 두 회사가 재결합하면 규모가 훨씬 커질 거예요.
examples.en: If the two companies that split up merge again, the scale will be much larger.

examples.ko: 저는 헤어진 사람과 재결합하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to get back together with someone I broke up with.

explain: 헤어진 연인에게는 '다시 만나다', '다시 사귀다'가 말할 때 더 자연스럽고, '재결합하다'는 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요. 그룹이나 회사가 다시 합칠 때도 써요. '하다'가 붙은 말이라 '재결합했어요'처럼 활용해요.
explain_en: For an ex-couple, 다시 만나다 or 다시 사귀다 sounds more natural in speech; 재결합하다 appears more in news and writing. It also covers groups or companies joining again. Conjugate it like other 하다 verbs: 재결합했어요.

examples.en: What type of car do you want to buy?
Insurance costs differ depending on the car model.

examples.ko: 이 주차장에는 큰 차종은 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Large car types cannot enter this parking lot.
I look at the color before the car model.
To get it repaired, please tell me the car model and year.
These days the number of electric car models has grown a lot.

explain: 차종은 '소나타', '아반떼'처럼 차의 이름이나 종류를 말해요. 정비소, 보험, 중고차 거래에서 '차종이 뭐예요?' 하고 자주 물어요. 차를 만든 회사는 '제조사', 만든 해는 '연식'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 차종 refers to the name or kind of a car, like 소나타 or 아반떼. At repair shops, insurance and used-car deals you often hear 차종이 뭐예요? The maker is 제조사 and the production year is 연식.

examples.en: I searched the grass for clovers for a long time.
A clover usually has three leaves.
My friend gave me a lucky clover ring as a gift.

examples.ko: 공원 잔디 사이에 하얀 클로버 꽃이 피었어요.
examples.en: White clover flowers bloomed among the park grass.
Where there is a lot of clover, there are also a lot of bees.

examples.ko: 카드 무늬 중에 클로버 모양도 있어요.
examples.en: Among the card suits, there is a clover shape too.

explain: 세 잎 클로버는 '행복', 네 잎 클로버는 '행운'이라고 말해요. 네 잎 클로버를 찾는 건 흔한 놀이예요. '네잎클로버'처럼 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: A three-leaf clover is said to mean '행복' (happiness) and a four-leaf clover '행운' (luck). Looking for a four-leaf clover is a common pastime. It is sometimes written as one word, '네잎클로버'.

examples.en: Two prisoners broke out of jail before dawn.

examples.ko: 영화에서 주인공이 탈옥하는 장면이 인상 깊었어요.
examples.en: The scene where the hero breaks out of prison stood out in the movie.

examples.ko: 그는 감옥에서 탈옥하려고 몇 년 동안 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: He planned for years to escape from prison.
I heard the escaped criminal was caught in two days.

examples.ko: 탈옥하고 나서도 마음 편히 지내지 못했어요.
examples.en: Even after escaping prison, he couldn't live in peace.

examples.ko: 탈옥할 방법이 없다는 걸 알고 포기했어요.
examples.en: He gave up when he realized there was no way to break out.

explain: 감옥에서 도망칠 때만 쓰고, 다른 곳에서 빠져나오는 건 '탈출하다'나 '도망치다'를 써요. 뉴스와 영화 줄거리에서 주로 보여요. 발음은 [타로카다]예요.
explain_en: It is only for escaping from a prison; for getting out of other places use '탈출하다' or '도망치다'. You mostly see it in the news and in movie plots. It is pronounced [타로카다].

en: with a light tap; with a pop

examples.en: My friend tapped me lightly on the shoulder.
The soda fizzes sharply in my mouth.
Flick off the dust and have a seat.
A drop of water plopped onto the window.
I nudged the ball lightly and it rolled away.
The berry burst with a pop.

explain: 작고 가벼운 것이 부딪히거나 터지는 소리와 모양을 나타내요. '톡 치다', '톡 털다', '톡 쏘다'처럼 짝이 정해진 동사가 많아요. 비슷한 '탁'은 더 세고 단단한 느낌이라서 '탁 치다'는 훨씬 강해요.
explain_en: Imitates the sound and look of something small and light hitting or popping. It pairs with set verbs such as '톡 치다' (tap), '톡 털다' (flick off) and '톡 쏘다' (sting/fizz). The similar '탁' feels harder and stronger, so '탁 치다' is much firmer.

examples.en: There are many windmills in the Netherlands.
When the wind blew, the windmill turned slowly.

examples.ko: 언덕 위에 낡은 풍차가 서 있어요.
examples.en: An old windmill stands on the hill.
The child bought a windmill-shaped toy.

examples.ko: 여행 책에서 풍차 마을 사진을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a picture of a windmill village in a travel book.
Don Quixote mistook windmills for giants.

explain: 전기를 만드는 현대 기계는 '풍력 발전기'라고 하고, '풍차'는 옛날 곡식을 빻거나 물을 푸던 모양의 건물에 어울려요. 사진이나 동화 속 풍차 마을을 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: A modern machine that makes electricity is a '풍력 발전기'; '풍차' fits the old-style structure used to grind grain or pump water. It is often used for windmill villages in photos and stories.

en: be unfrozen; be defrosted; be thawed

examples.en: The frozen shrimp haven't thawed yet.
Meat thaws quickly if you leave it at room temperature.
Frozen bread gets soft once it thaws.
Please wash the fish once it is fully thawed.

examples.ko: 전자레인지에서 밥이 해동되는 데 삼 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes three minutes for rice to defrost in the microwave.
I took it out in the morning and it was fully thawed by evening.

explain: '해동되다'는 음식이 녹아서 풀린 결과에 초점이 있어요. 하는 사람이 보일 때는 '해동하다'를 써요. '고기가 해동됐어요'와 '고기를 해동했어요'를 구별해 보세요.
explain_en: '해동되다' focuses on the result: food that has thawed. When a person does the thawing, use '해동하다'. Compare '고기가 해동됐어요' with '고기를 해동했어요'.
